title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure / IaC, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also catalogues canonical ADRs relevant to these areas and provides templates for new ADRs and change proposals. The goal is to provide a single authoritative reference for design reviews, onboarding, and cross-team consistency.

Scope

- Applies to all backend services, inference runtimes, control plane components, and customer-facing APIs.
- Includes hosted, dedicated, and private/private-control-plane deployments.
- Excludes UI style guidelines (handled in frontend-design repo) and marketing content.

Principles

1. Predictability: APIs and runtimes should have clear performance and cost expectations (SLOs/SALs).
2. Observability-first: All services must emit standardized metrics and traces before rollout.
3. Reproducibility: Infrastructure and model packaging are codified (IaC + image manifests).
4. Backwards compatibility and safe rollouts: Versioning + canary/A-B + automatic fallback.
5. Security & least privilege: Secrets, KMS, and RBAC are mandatory for private deployments.

1) API Standards

Purpose: Keep client integration simple and durable across model and infra changes.

API Naming and Structure
- Use RESTful resources for control-plane endpoints and gRPC for internal high-throughput RPCs. Public inference surface is HTTP/JSON.
- Use hyphen-separated paths and nouns: /v1/models/{model-id}/infer
- Versioning: major version in path (e.g., /v1/). Minor changes use content negotiation with an explicit "model-spec" header.

Request/Response Best Practices
- Use clear, typed JSON schemas. Attach canonical examples to API spec.
- Responses MUST include a trace_id header for cross-service correlation: X-Request-Id or X-Redwood-Trace.
- Streaming: adopt chunked-transfer encoding with application/json-seq for streaming tokens.

Errors and Status Codes
- Standardize error envelope: {"code": "string", "message": "string", "details": [...] }
- Map categories to HTTP codes: 4xx for client, 429 for rate limits, 5xx for transient server issues. Provide retriable flag in details.

Rate Limiting and Quotas
- Token-based usage quota model. Endpoints must return X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.
- Clients should be informed of backoff strategy in 429 details.

Auth and Authorization
- OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens for hosted API; mutual TLS optionally for dedicated/private control plane.
- Per-route RBAC claim mapping. Keys managed via KMS integrations for private deployments.

API Examples and Schema (snippet)

```json
POST /v1/models/redwood-7b/infer
Headers: {"Authorization": "Bearer <token>", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
Body: {"input": "Summarize: ...", "max_tokens": 128, "stream": true}

Response chunk (stream): {"id":"token","text":"The summary...","token_index": 42}
```

2) Coding Standards

Languages & Repos
- Backend core services: Go (runtime, infra control-plane), Python (model onboarding, evals), Rust (hot paths optional).
- SDKs: TypeScript, Python, Go. Separate repos per SDK with shared CI.

Formatting and Linters
- Go: gofmt, golangci-lint (enabled linters: govet, staticcheck, errcheck).
- Python: black, ruff, mypy strict-checking for public packages.
- TypeScript: eslint + prettier with the company config.

PR and Review Rules
1. Small, single-purpose PRs (<= 400 lines where possible).
2. Required checks: unit tests, linter, integration smoke, and one reviewer from owning team.
3. All public API changes require an ADR and a migration plan.

Testing and CI
- Unit tests must run in < 2 minutes on CI. Integration tests for model-serving must run in dedicated runners with GPU emulation or small real-GPU pools.
- Use canary pipelines for infra changes with automatic rollback on health regressions.

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC, Networking, Secrets)

IaC and Environments
- Terraform for cloud infra; state stored in encrypted remote backend (S3 + DynamoDB or equivalent).
- Environment tiers: dev, staging, prod. Staging mirrors prod network topology and data flows.

Image and Packaging
- Build immutable images; tag with semantic version + git sha: service:v{major}.{minor}.{patch}-{sha}.
- For private/on-prem, supply an OCI image bundle + manifest file and a signed release artifact.

Secrets and Keys
- Use KMS for key material; never store secrets in plaintext. Use HashiCorp Vault or cloud-native secret manager with tight ACLs.

Network and Multi-region
- Services must be region-aware. Cross-region failover is supported for hosted and dedicated tiers; private deployments must present RTO requirements at onboarding.

4) Model-Serving Standards

Model Packaging and Versioning
- Package models with manifest.json including: model_id, version, architecture, tokenizer_spec, quantization_profile, expected_memory_gpu_mb, kv_cache_behavior.
- Semantic model versioning: MAJOR for incompatible changes in tokenizer/metadata, MINOR for performance/optimization, PATCH for bugfixes.

Quantization and Compatibility
- Quantization profiles are documented in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Each profile includes: supported hardware, expected quality delta (per-eval), memory savings.

Rollouts and Safety
- Canary rollout procedure: 1) deploy model variant to 1–5% traffic, 2) monitor latency/quality for 2–4 hours, 3) expand to 25% then 100% if green. Automatic rollback on SLI breach.
- Provide a fallback mapping layer: if a variant fails, requests automatically route to a compatible baseline model.

Evaluation and Quality Gates
- All model deploys must pass a predefined eval suite (per-customer prompt set where applicable). Failure to meet baseline triggers blocked rollout.

5) Observability Standards

Metrics (Prometheus style)
- Required metrics: request_rate, token_output_rate, latency_p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms), failed_requests, model_cache_hit_ratio, batch_size_mean, gpu_utilization.
- Metric naming: service.component.metric (e.g., runtime.infer.latency_p99_ms).

Tracing
- Use OpenTelemetry (OTel) for distributed tracing. Ensure spans include model_id, model_version, batch_id, and hardware_region attributes.

Logs
- Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, span_id, trace_id, msg, metadata. Logs must not contain PII or customer prompt content unless explicitly obfuscated and approved.

Dashboards and Alerts
- Per-service dashboards: throughput, latency percentiles, error rate, and cost counters.
- Standard alerts: high-error-rate (>0.5% over 5m), p99 latency breach (>2x SLO over 5m), GPU OOM events. Alert runbooks must be linked on each dashboard.

SLOs and SLIs
- Default inference SLOs (hosted API): availability 99.95% monthly; latency p99 <= 1200ms for small models (<= 7B) and p99 <= 2500ms for medium models (7B–70B). SLOs are configurable per-tier for Dedicated.
- Expose objective and burn-rate dashboards; maintain error budget ownership per service.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarking

Load Testing
- Every major change to runtime, kernel, or batching should be validated via the benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Tests must include: steady-state throughput, cold-start latency, KV-cache hit-patterns, and worst-case sequence lengths.

Cost Metrics
- Track tokens-per-dollar per model variant. Maintain a performance/cost dashboard comparing baseline open models with optimized variants.

Profiling and Optimization
- Use GPU-level profilers (Nsight, Triton traces) and runtime flamegraphs. Document heavy kernels and provide optimization notes in kernel-and-scheduling.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)

ADR Template
- ID: ADR-YYYY-NN
- Title: short name
- Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated
- Context: problem statement and background
- Decision: chosen approach
- Consequences: operational and technical implications
- Owner: individual or team
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD

Canonical ADRs (summaries)
1) ADR-2024-07: HTTP vs gRPC for inference control-plane
   - Decision: Use HTTP/JSON for public inference APIs; gRPC for internal high-throughput services.
   - Rationale: compatibility and streaming ergonomics for clients vs efficiency for internal RPCs.
   - Consequences: Maintain both stacks, provide SDK mapping layers.

2) ADR-2025-01: Model versioning semantics
   - Decision: Semantic model versions (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) + manifest.json required.
   - Consequences: Enforced model registry checks, upgrade paths.

3) ADR-2025-11: Default SLO targets for hosted API
   - Decision: availability 99.95%, p99 latency thresholds as described above.

Adding a new ADR (procedure)
1. Create ADR markdown using template; assign owner.
2. Publish to /confluence/architecture-and-standards and open PR in adr-repo.
3. Notify reviewers and allow 7 business days for comments.
4. Once accepted, update related-service runbooks and deployment pipelines (link ADR ID in CI job).

Operational Runbooks and Owners
- Every service must have a runbook in confluence/eng-platform/runbooks and an on-call owner listed. Runbooks should include: common failure modes, mitigation steps, and escalation contacts.
- Example owner: runtime-inference-service -> owner_team: eng-serving-runtime, oncall_contact: #sre-runtime.

Governance and Change Control
- Breaking API or ADR-level decisions require stakeholder review from product, security, and at least two engineering leads.
- Major infra or model-serving changes must go through game-day simulation in staging with a documented rollback plan.

Appendices

Appendix A — API error envelope example
| field | type | description |
|---|---:|---|
| code | string | machine-readable error code (e.g. RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) |
| message | string | human-friendly message |
| retriable | boolean | whether clients should retry |

Appendix B — ADR index (links)
- ADR-2024-07: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-2024-07-http-vs-grpc.json
- ADR-2025-01: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-2025-01-model-versioning.json
- ADR-2025-11: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-2025-11-default-slos.json
